subject.title: Memory/QMD: isolate mcporter sidecars per agent

question: Should OpenClaw permanently own generated per-agent MCPorter config and daemon identity for bare QMD stdio definitions while leaving every customized or credential-bearing definition under its discovered user config?
rationale: The implementation is coherent, but this generated-versus-external split establishes a long-lived ownership and upgrade contract that tests alone cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve the split
options.body: Adopt the generated-only-for-bare rule, then require a rebase and exact-head fresh-install and upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow to env isolation
options.body: Keep user MCPorter config authoritative for every server and land only the smaller QMD-versus-MCPorter process-environment separation.

options.title: Pause generated ownership
options.body: Do not merge this branch until a different canonical sidecar ownership design is agreed.

recommendation.title: Approve the split
recommendation.body: Adopt the generated-only-for-bare rule, then require a rebase and exact-head fresh-install and upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work provides the strongest continuing ownership signal across QMD routing, compatibility, and manager tests.
